A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same consistency metrics and ranking-based data refinement framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations, instruction-tuning experiments and downstream ranking results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds MS MARCO experiments, size-matched training comparisons, ranking-estimator comparisons and a subgraph-size sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: The original win-loss aggregation, pairwise extrapolation and negated-relation augmentation pipeline remains, now named REPAIR. Appendix N adds evaluated variants substituting Elo or Bradley-Terry for win-loss aggregation, a limited adaptation of one component.

E1.justification: Appendices B and L add MS MARCO query–passage data for REPAIR training and evaluation, extending the intervention beyond summarization. Document reranking was already represented by NovelEval, and all original datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: v1 mentions Elo and Bradley-Terry as possible alternatives; v3 actually compares both against win-loss aggregation in Table 7. The original LLM comparator roster remains; Deepseek-chat-v2 clarifies the model already associated with the DeepSeek-v2 citation.

E3.justification: v3 adds training-data-size controls, a subgraph-size sweep and an MS MARCO protocol using 800 training and 200 test examples with ten retrieved candidates and GPT-3.5-derived rankings. Figure 7 also revises the existing SummEval prompt to require only A or B; the PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to subgraph size K (Appendix H), whether consistency gains persist after matching training-set sizes (Appendix M), and dependence on the ranking estimator (Appendix N). These address methodological questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Appendix I adds a binomial/normal-approximation sample-size argument at 95% confidence for the existing M=1000 sampling cap, although the numerical error margin is unspecified. The existing ten CoT samples, 100 PairS runs and correlation significance reporting remain unchanged; no new empirical uncertainty estimates are provided.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–5 retain their values. v3 adds substantial results in Tables 5–7 and Figure 9: for example, Table 5 reports MS MARCO transitivity of 86.7 versus 91.3 and PairS scores of 58.1 versus 61.0 for perturbed versus REPAIR training. v1's reported correlations below 0.05 between transitivity and human accuracy are removed.

T1.justification: v3 adds the sample-size reasoning in Equation 4, explicitly discusses the irreflexive assumption in Appendix J, and supplies analytical examples of ranking-rule limitations in Appendix N. The original consistency definitions and graph algorithms remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refocus broad logical-consistency and overall-robustness claims on logical preference consistency and judgment robustness. The four principal contributions, alignment-preservation claim and downstream-performance claim remain; the conclusion still uses broader reliability language.

C2.justification: Appendices H, M and N add substantive guidance on choosing K, attribute alignment losses after downsampling to information loss, and discuss aggregation limitations involving indirect comparisons, ordering and ties. Section 3.3 also changes the interpretation of transitivity from a proxy for global reliability to one for local robustness.

D1.justification: Appendix G supplies previously missing NovelEval, CaTeRS and instruction-tuning prompt templates, plus explicit metric-computation instructions. Appendix B documents MS MARCO preparation and label provenance. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the existing LoRA settings, hardware description and ANONYMOUS code/data placeholder remain.

R1.justification: Appendix E adds a focused distinction from social-network clustering, triad census and E-I measures with supporting citations. Additional references support sampling theory, Elo and MS MARCO, while some instruction-tuning background references disappear. The main positioning against factual-knowledge and NLI consistency research remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion and several main-text passages are substantially condensed or rewritten, with revised preference-consistency terminology and REPAIR naming throughout. The original Section 4 motivation moves to Appendix K, the downstream subsection is consolidated, and the appendix organization expands considerably.

P2.justification: The main text and bibliography change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 7 expands into a three-task prompt grid, and v3 adds Figures 8–9 and Tables 5–7.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked a control for increased training-data volume and assessed downstream benefits by comparing different pretrained models. v3's size-matched ablation (Table 6) and training-to-downstream experiment (Table 5) address these important validation gaps, while sensitivity tests and fuller prompts strengthen assessment and reproducibility. The gains remain qualified by GPT-derived MS MARCO labels and unexplained baseline differences between Table 3 and Tables 6–7.
